clue.text: Chelsea's game at Old Trafford is off

definitions.meaning: Old Trafford is Manchester United's football ground, so a Chelsea match there is played on the road, not at home
gone, not here, as in 'she is off on holiday'

explanation.surface: A football fan learns that Chelsea's fixture in Manchester has been called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is off' reads as a cancellation, but 'off' is a second definition: absent. Old Trafford is the home ground of Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixture played on the opponent's ground is called this, and the same word means absent or gone.

clue.text: The element against funds not having European investment

parts.note: anti- means opposed to, against

indicators.note: signals that a letter is taken out of the word for funds

parts.note: money is funds
E is the abbreviation for European, here the letter invested in the word for funds

explanation.surface: An investor complains about funds that refuse to back European ventures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having' takes E out of MONEY to leave MONY.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimony is a metalloid chemical element, symbol Sb, so it is an example of an element.

clue.text: Scoffed about story not applicable to divorce

indicators.note: the word for scoffed goes around the other pieces, as about can mean surrounding

parts.note: to scoff food is to eat it greedily, so scoffed means ate
a lie is a made-up story
NA is the standard abbreviation for not applicable on forms

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a tale that has nothing to do with a marriage break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' looks like mocking; here it means eating greedily. 'divorce' is a verb meaning to separate.
explanation.definitionFit: To divorce something is to separate or estrange it, which is what alienate means in its transitive sense.

clue.text: Weighty exercise found in papers on work table?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece put on another follows it

parts.note: a bench is a work table, as in a carpenter's bench
the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: A gym instruction suggests lifting weights while lying on a workbench covered in newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'work table' is a playful way to describe a bench, with the papers sitting on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The bench press is a weightlifting exercise in which a barbell is pushed up while lying on a bench.

clue.text: Bug a naughty child's decapitated

indicators.note: having its head cut off, so the first letter of the word for the child goes

parts.note: a badly behaved child is called a little terror; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered remark wishing a troublesome child would lose his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitated' removes the first letter T from TERROR.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug in software is a fault or mistake, so the two words are synonyms in computing.

clue.text: Pass level given by fellow member of staff

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a league is a level or class of competition, as in 'not in the same league'

explanation.surface: An employee is given a pass mark by a co-worker of equal standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague is someone who works alongside you, a fellow employee in the same organisation.

clue.text: It's pretty neat especially as a way to identify the old man

definitions.text: a way to identify the old man

indicators.note: read as 'specially', made up specially, so the letters of the preceding words are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Praise for something tidy and clever, admired as a means of recognising an elderly gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'especially' is the signal for rearranging all of IT'S PRETTY NEAT. 'The old man' is slang for father.
explanation.definitionFit: A DNA check of who fathered a child is a means of establishing someone's father, informally the old man.

clue.text: Privileged former politician to appear in film

parts.note: ex- means former

indicators.note: the politician's letters go inside the film's title

parts.note: ET is the 1982 Spielberg film E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A one-time MP with special status lands a role in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to appear in' is the container signal, putting the politician inside the film title.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exempt means being freed from a duty others must bear, a privileged status.

clue.text: Saw right through pipe

indicators.note: the letters for right run through the middle of the word for pipe

parts.note: to pipe is to sing in a high voice, as birds do
ay (aye) is an exclamation of agreement, like 'right!'

explanation.surface: A plumber's cutting tool goes right through a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the tool or the past of see; it is a noun for a proverb. 'through' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, as in 'the old saw'.

clue.text: Tourist — one giving baksheesh without resistance

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the word for the giver goes around the other letter

parts.note: baksheesh is a tip or gratuity, so one who gives it is a tipper
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A tourist abroad hands out tips without meeting any opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but here means outside: TIPPER surrounds R.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripper is a person on a pleasure trip, especially a day trip, so a tourist.

clue.text: After treatment in here a pet dog could be timid

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are treated, that is processed into a new order

explanation.surface: A vet notes that a pet dog might be nervous after being treated here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After treatment' rearranges the letters of IN HERE A PET DOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigeon-hearted means having the courage of a pigeon, so cowardly or easily frightened.

clue.text: Draw animal in extremely lovely location

indicators.note: the animal is placed inside the outer letters
takes the extreme, first and last, letters of lovely

parts.note: an otter is an animal

explanation.surface: An artist sketches an animal in a beautiful spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like a verb about sketching; it is a noun for a prize draw. 'extremely' gives L and Y, with OTTER put in between; 'location' completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is a draw in which tickets are picked at random to decide prizes.

clue.text: Blokes I agree when drunk are a strange collection of people

parts.note: blokes is British slang for men

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters reel about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of men, tipsy and agreeing with everything, make an odd crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when drunk' rearranges I AGREE into AGERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a collection of wild animals, a menagerie is used figuratively for a diverse or strange group of people.

clue.text: Split's close to this city

parts.note: a rip is a split or tear
on can mean near or close to, as in 'a house on the river'

explanation.surface: Split, the Croatian port, is said to lie near this city.
explanation.walkthrough: Split looks like the Croatian city; it is a tear. RIPON is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripon is a cathedral city in North Yorkshire, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Subject: where motor-race starts — plenty of power here

parts.note: a subject of a state is a national, a citizen
cars line up on the starting grid before a motor race

explanation.surface: A racing commentator names the topic: the starting line-up, where the energy is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' reads as a topic heading; it is a noun for a citizen. The National Grid is Britain's electricity transmission network.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Grid is the network carrying electricity across Britain, so lots of power is found on it.

clue.text: Having relations with collaborator makes one a laughing stock

parts.note: aunts are relations
an ally is a collaborator or partner

explanation.surface: Someone caught in an affair with an accomplice becomes the butt of jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having relations' hints at an affair; here it simply supplies relatives. An Aunt Sally is a British fairground target at which sticks are thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunt Sally, from a fairground throwing game, means a person set up as a target for ridicule.

clue.text: Express at rear of platform two finally departed

indicators.note: tells us the deletion happens at the back end of the word for platform
the chosen letter leaves, so it is taken out

parts.note: a manifesto is a party's political platform

indicators.note: takes the last letter of the word two

explanation.surface: A train announcement: the express at the back of platform two has finally left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like the train; it is a verb. 'finally' gives O, the last letter of two, which 'departed' removes from the end ('at rear of') of MANIFESTO.
explanation.definitionFit: To manifest a feeling is to show or display it, which is to express it.

clue.text: Overruled what the answer to the final clue might be

definitions.meaning: a decision overturned by a higher authority, as on appeal

definitions.text: what the answer to the final clue might be
definitions.meaning: the last clue in the list is 23 Down, whose solution reads the same backwards, so it can be turned round without change

explanation.surface: A self-referential note that a decision was overturned, as the final clue's solution might be.
explanation.walkthrough: The final clue printed is 23 Down, a word that is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruling that is overturned on appeal is said to have been reversed by the higher court.

clue.text: Tube station nearly destroyed in accident

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for accident

parts.note: chance is accident, as in 'by chance'

indicators.note: the letters of nearly are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A report that an Underground station was almost wrecked in a mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' looks like an adverb; it is the fodder. 'destroyed' rearranges NEARLY into ERYLAN, which goes 'in' CHANCE. Chancery Lane is a London Underground station.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancery Lane is a station on the Central line of the London Underground, known as the Tube.

clue.text: Prepare for eg running battle with half-cut fool

parts.note: war is battle

indicators.note: half-cut is British slang for drunk, but here it means cut in half, so only the front half of the word for fool is kept

parts.note: a muppet is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a running fight alongside a tipsy idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' reads as drunk; it keeps MUP, the first half of MUPPET.
explanation.definitionFit: To warm up is to do gentle exercise to get ready for a race or other physical activity.

clue.text: Long range signal originally heard on the radio?

definitions.meaning: a long jagged chain of mountains

definitions.text: signal originally heard on the radio?
definitions.meaning: the first letter of signal is S, and radio operators say S using the code word for that letter

explanation.surface: An operator asks whether a long-distance signal was first picked up over the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long range' reads as distance; it is a mountain range. In the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for S is the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long mountain range with a jagged profile, and also the radio code word for the letter S.

clue.text: A small cat and a dog

parts.note: a kit is a kitten, a small cat

explanation.surface: A list of pets: a kitten and a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Akita is a large Japanese breed of dog, so it is an example of a dog.

clue.text: Work for a spell as one behind bars may do

definitions.meaning: to put in a period of duty, as in serving time in the army

definitions.text: as one behind bars may do
definitions.meaning: a prisoner behind bars spends a sentence in jail

explanation.surface: Putting in a stint of work, the way a prisoner does.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve time means to undergo a prison sentence, and loosely to work a stint in a job.

clue.text: Send up and down

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word reads the same going up as going down

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An instruction to dispatch something both upwards and downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer someone to a specialist is to send them there.

clue.text: Almost spoil everything to do with couple's relationship

indicators.note: nearly all of the phrase, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: to spoil everything is to mar it all

explanation.surface: A warning that someone is close to ruining their marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last L from MAR IT ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital means relating to marriage, the relationship between a married couple.

clue.text: Competence revealed by match point

parts.note: to fit is to match, as in 'the key fits the lock'
a ness is a headland or point, as in Orford Ness on the Suffolk coast

explanation.surface: A tennis player's skill shows itself at match point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match point' reads as tennis; the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitness for a role means being suitable and capable, so it is a synonym for competence.

clue.text: Pyramid Club shortly organised a party in UK

indicators.note: the letters are organised, put into a new arrangement
cut short, so the last letter of club is dropped

explanation.surface: A pyramid-selling club has set up a political party in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims B from CLUB; 'organised' rearranges PYRAMID CLU. Plaid Cymru is the Welsh nationalist party.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid Cymru is a political party in Wales, part of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Boss gambling with cards

definitions.meaning: a boss is an ornamental knob or ... on a surface
a form of poker in which some cards are dealt face up

explanation.surface: The boss plays poker.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a raised knob, the same as a boss, and stud poker is a card game.
